card.name: Conga line
card.tagline: Carnival processional line dance from Cuba.
card.profile: The conga line is a novelty line dance derived from the Cuban carnival conga (comparsa) of Santiago de Cuba, where neighborhood comparsas march in serpentine processions (arrollando) descended from Afro-Cuban Congolese cabildos. Dancers form a line, each holding the waist of the person ahead, with three shuffle steps and a kick on the fourth beat, to a staccato conga-drum rhythm (plus the corneta china in Santiago). It became a US craze in the 1930s-1950s, popularized by Desi Arnaz and Xavier Cugat (English Wikipedia; Harvard ReVista).
card.insight: The conga was one of the earliest successful 20th-century Cuban musical exports, helping prepare international audiences for son, mambo and salsa - even as it was banned at times in Cuba as a dangerous mass gathering (English Wikipedia; Harvard ReVista).
